content.title: About
content.content: Unsweetened applesauce is a 100 % pure puree made from ripe apples, prepared without added sugar, sweeteners, or preservatives. It has a smooth texture and a mildly tart flavor, suitable for both children and adults.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Applesauce is often used as a first solid food for infants after breast‑milk or formula.
In the United States and Canada, applesauce is a common component of school lunch programs.
Unsweetened varieties retain most of the vitamins and dietary fiber found in fresh apples.
Apples are among the world’s most widely cultivated fruits, with over 80 million tonnes of puree produced annually.
The production process involves heat treatment that eliminates pathogens while preserving the apple aroma.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Applesauce provides vitamin C, which supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: The puree retains pectin and fiber that promote healthy digestion and help regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Without added sugar, applesauce contains about 45 kcal per 100 g, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Flavonoids and polyphenols in apples help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Pectin may help lower LDL (bad) cholesterol levels.

items.title: Apple allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to apples, ranging from itching to swelling or hives.

items.title: Natural sugar content
items.content: Although no sugar is added, the puree contains natural fruit sugars, which should be considered by people with diabetes.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic pH can irritate a sensitive stomach in some individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Unsweetened applesauce can be enjoyed on its own, mixed into oatmeal, yogurt, smoothies, baked goods, or used as a base for sauces and desserts. For infants, it is often served slightly warmed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: After opening, keep the puree in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 7 days. Unopened packages should be stored in a cool, dry place away from direct light.
